name: Outlines
notable_features: Schema-driven structured generation whose stated thesis is that post-hoc parsing, regex munging and fragile retry code are the wrong shape - the constraint should be in the sampler, not after it
The README's portability claim is 'same code runs across OpenAI, Ollama, vLLM and more', i.e. it works as a remote client against a hosted model as well as in-process against a local one
Pure Python (Nix is the only other language in the repo), which makes it the most readable of the three structured-generation libraries
Handles regular expressions, JSON Schema and finite-state-style grammars as first-class constraint types
Widely adopted as a library rather than a server: the README lists NVIDIA, Cohere, HuggingFace and vLLM among organisations using it
v1.x line now (1.3.3 on 2026-08-06), 15897 stars, 906 open issues
hardware_caveats: Same category boundary as XGrammar: this is a library a serving stack imports, not an engine. scheduling is 'none' and supported_backends reflects host reach only

Pure-Python constraint machinery on the per-token critical path is materially slower than a C++ core. In vLLM/SGLang the fix is that you use XGrammar there instead (see [[niche-xgrammar]]), which is precisely why Outlines is no longer the default structured backend in those servers

The 'works with any model' claim is true for OpenAI-compatible remote endpoints and weaker for exotic local engines - you need a logits-level hook, which rules out most llama.cpp builds unless a specific integration exists

REPO MOVE WARNING: the project left the outlines-dev org. github.com/outlines-dev/outlines returns HTTP 200 after redirecting to dottxt-ai/outlines, so pre-2024 citations still resolve, but the owner path changed and dependency pins referencing 'outlines-dev' are stale
906 open issues against 15897 stars is a high open-issue ratio for a library; the issue backlog is the practical signal about support burden
Layered on top of a host model, so every host-engine caveat inherits: a bad logit-processing path on a niche backend breaks constrained output too
best_for: Rapid prototyping of schema-constrained generation, especially when you want to iterate on the constraint in Python without touching a C++ build
Local model work where you control the host process and can install a logits hook
Learning the design space of structured generation - the constraint types and the failure modes are all readable in one Python repo
avoid_for: Latency-critical per-token constraint checking in production - use the C++ path (XGrammar) via vLLM or SGLang
Remote/hosted models behind a plain HTTP API with no logits exposure
New dependency pins that name the old outlines-dev org
notes: Third of three structured-generation records (with [[niche-xgrammar]] and [[niche-lm-format-enforcer]]). The three differ in mechanism and in current relevance: XGrammar is the production default in vLLM/SGLang, lm-format-enforcer was vLLM's previous default, and Outlines is the most readable and the least performance-oriented.
